title: Build domain expert agents on pi
topic: Building domain-specific expert agents on the pi coding agent
summary: Starting from what an agent harness is, you learn how the open-source pi coding agent is built and which of its parts turn it into a specialist. You build a shared base pack and three experts, an SQL analyst, a Kubernetes operator and a quant researcher, each boxed in, measured with evals, and reached through one router.

concepts.name: Language model
concepts.summary: A language model writes text by predicting one likely next piece at a time.

concepts.name: The context window
concepts.summary: A model can only read a fixed number of tokens in one request.

concepts.name: Tool call
concepts.summary: Instead of text, a model can reply with a request to run a named function with arguments.

concepts.name: The agent loop
concepts.summary: A program repeats model request, tool run and result until the model answers in text.

concepts.name: Agent harness
concepts.summary: The harness owns the loop, the tools, the instructions and the record, while the model only predicts.

concepts.name: Session log
concepts.summary: Every message and tool result is written to a file, so a conversation can be read back and resumed.

concepts.name: Package layers
concepts.summary: pi splits into pi-ai for models, pi-agent-core for the loop and pi-coding-agent for sessions, tools and the command line.

concepts.name: The pi loop
concepts.summary: pi's loop runs until the model makes no tool call, a hook ends the turn or the run is aborted.

concepts.name: Tool batch
concepts.summary: Tool calls from one reply run in parallel, and one sequential tool makes the whole batch run in order.

concepts.name: Session tree
concepts.summary: Each entry names its parent, so branching only moves the leaf, and the model sees the path from root to leaf.

concepts.name: Prompt patch
concepts.summary: pi stores the prompt and the tool list as system messages, and later messages replace named sections.

concepts.name: Context projection
concepts.summary: Some entries are logged but hidden from the model, and edits change what it sees without changing the log.

concepts.name: Provider
concepts.summary: Every provider fills one interface, and DeepSeek runs over the OpenAI-compatible adapter with its own thinking format.

concepts.name: Compaction
concepts.summary: When tokens pass the window minus a reserve, pi summarises older entries and keeps about 20,000 recent tokens.

concepts.name: Domain expert
concepts.summary: An expert is pi with one role, a small set of tools, its own knowledge and checks for one domain.

concepts.name: Expert prompt
concepts.summary: --system-prompt replaces pi's preamble, --append-system-prompt adds an addendum, and SYSTEM.md files do the same without flags.

concepts.name: Context files
concepts.summary: pi loads AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md from its own folder and from every parent folder, root first.

concepts.name: Skill
concepts.summary: Only a skill's name and description sit in the prompt, and the model reads the full SKILL.md when a task needs it.

concepts.name: Prompt template
concepts.summary: A Markdown file becomes a slash command, with $1 and $@ filled from what the user types.

concepts.name: Agent folder
concepts.summary: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR moves settings, sessions, MCP config and credentials, so each expert gets its own.

concepts.name: Settings layers
concepts.summary: Global and project settings merge, project lists replace global ones, and project files load only when trusted.

concepts.name: Package
concepts.summary: A package bundles extensions, skills, prompts and themes and installs from npm, git or a folder.

concepts.name: Extension
concepts.summary: An extension's default export takes the pi API and registers tools, commands and event handlers.

concepts.name: Custom tool
concepts.summary: A tool has a TypeBox schema and an execute function that returns content for the model and details for your code.

concepts.name: Tight schema
concepts.summary: pi checks every call against its schema first, so enums, limits and no extra fields stop bad calls early.

concepts.name: Tool allowlist
concepts.summary: --tools and --exclude-tools choose the active tools, and a tool with a built-in's name replaces it.

concepts.name: MCP server
concepts.summary: Servers in mcp.json give tools named mcp__server__tool, exposed directly, on search, through codemode or not at all.

concepts.name: Codemode
concepts.summary: The model writes JavaScript that runs in a QuickJS sandbox and calls tools through the normal pipeline.

concepts.name: Call gate
concepts.summary: A tool_call handler can change the arguments or return block with a reason, and a handler that throws also blocks.

concepts.name: Result rewrite
concepts.summary: A tool_result handler can replace the content, details or error flag, for example to hide secrets.

concepts.name: Headless approval
concepts.summary: With no screen, confirm returns false, so an unattended expert must deny risky calls instead of asking.

concepts.name: Security boundary
concepts.summary: pi has no sandbox: bash is a plain spawn with your full environment, so safety comes from limiting what the process can reach.

concepts.name: Expert container
concepts.summary: Running pi inside a container with only the expert's folder mounted is the strongest practical boundary.

concepts.name: Bash backend
concepts.summary: BashOperations replaces where bash runs, so commands can go over SSH or into a container.

concepts.name: Environment scrub
concepts.summary: bash passes the whole parent environment, so a spawnHook gives each command only the variables it needs.

concepts.name: Golden task
concepts.summary: A golden task fixes the starting files and the outcome a correct expert leaves behind.

concepts.name: Faux provider
concepts.summary: pi-ai's faux provider plays scripted replies and tool calls, so tests of an expert run without a real model.

concepts.name: Outcome grader
concepts.summary: Graders check the files, query results or tool calls the expert left, not what its reply claims.

concepts.name: Eval runner
concepts.summary: A runner gives each task a fresh folder and agent folder, runs pi, grades it and saves the session.

concepts.name: Lift
concepts.summary: Each task runs with and without the pack, and lift is the pass rate with it minus the pass rate without it.

concepts.name: Repeated runs
concepts.summary: Runs repeat in alternating order, and flaky or saturated results are flagged instead of averaged away.

concepts.name: Expert metrics
concepts.summary: getSessionStats gives tokens, tool calls and cost for each run, which you tag by expert.

concepts.name: Run mode
concepts.summary: pi runs once and prints, streams JSON lines, stays up as an RPC process or lives inside your program, each at a different cost.

concepts.name: RPC mode
concepts.summary: Commands and events are JSON lines over stdin and stdout, and a prompt is done at agent_settled, not when it is accepted.

concepts.name: SDK session
concepts.summary: createAgentSession takes a loader, tools, a model and a session folder, so one program can hold several experts.

concepts.name: Base pack
concepts.summary: A shared package holds house rules, common guards and logging, and each domain pack adds only what differs.

concepts.name: Router
concepts.summary: A router classifies a task, picks an expert, logs the choice and asks the user when it is unsure.

concepts.name: Handoff
concepts.summary: One expert's result becomes the next expert's task, as in the chain mode of pi's subagent example.

concepts.name: The SQL analyst
concepts.summary: A pack with a read-only query tool, schema skills and graders that compare query results.

concepts.name: The Kubernetes operator
concepts.summary: A pack whose guard allows reads, gates changes and refuses deletes, tested on a local cluster.

concepts.name: The quant researcher
concepts.summary: A pack whose codemode scripts run backtests and whose graders check numbers, not prose.

concepts.name: The expert fleet
concepts.summary: Router, base pack, three experts, containers and evals traced through one task.
